name: Amsterdam Albatross
rangeDescription: Breeds amsterdam island (french subantarctic islands)
description: Extremely rare. A huge Wandering-type albatross that breeds only on Amsterdam Island in the southern Indian Ocean, with only a handful of records elsewhere (mainly Australia).

name: Gray-backed Tachuri
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (central bahia to minas gerais and northern são paulo)
description: A small rare and endemic flycatcher with a conspicuous white patch in front of the eyes and a short white eyebrow. Also note its gray crown and a brownish-gray back and cinnamon washed breast and sides.

name: Great Thick-knee
rangeDescription: Southeastern iran to indian subcontinent, indochina, and hainan
description: An odd-looking wader with a dark mask, staring pale eyes, and a large heavy bill. Flashing black-and-white wingtips, revealed in flight, recall those of lapwings.

name: Roberts's Warbler
rangeDescription: Highland forest of eastern zimbabwe and adjacent southwestern mozambique
description: A dull gray-brown prinia-like warbler with a long and graduated tail, pale gray throat, ochre eyes, and pinkish legs. Pairs and family groups may join mixed-species flocks, foraging studiously through the lower branches of forest, undergrowth and bracken, forest edge, and occasionally pausing to chatter in unison.

name: Black-backed Water-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Amazonian and eastern brazil to eastern bolivia, paraguay, and northern argentina
description: Medium-sized flycatcher, usually seen walking on the ground around marshy areas, lakes, and rivers. Mostly white below and on the face contrasting with a black crown and back, a white rump and two white wingbars.

name: Crimson-breasted Gonolek
rangeDescription: Southwestern angola and namibia to botswana and northwestern south africa
description: A striking black-and-crimson bushshrike with a white stripe on its wing; a rare morph with yellow underparts also occurs. Singles and pairs forage alone or sometimes in mixed-species flocks in dry thornveld and dense tangles, where they prefer foraging on thicker trunks but will also forage on the open ground.

name: Venezuelan Wood-Quail
rangeDescription: Western venezuela (southwestern táchira) and coastal cordillera eastward to miranda
description: A robust and beautiful forest-dwelling quail with a short crest and a stout bill. Mostly rufous-brown body, boldly scaled white below and streaked white above.
imageCreditName: Jhonathan Miranda - Wandering Venezuela Birding Expeditions

name: West African Crested Tern
rangeDescription: Coastal mauritania to guinea; winters to namibia
description: A large tern found strictly in coastal areas. Very pale, with a long forked tail.

name: Giant Coua
rangeDescription: Thinly distributed in forest and savanna of western and southern madagascar
description: Huge, long-tailed, long-legged bird. Rufous belly and blue-and-pink bare facial skin.

name: Starry Owlet-nightjar
rangeDescription: Lowlands of central and eastern new guinea
description: A large owlet-nightjar found very locally in the forests of low hills. Bright rufous with 3 vertical bands on the underparts.

name: Iberian Gray Shrike
rangeDescription: Iberian peninsula and southern france
description: Thrush-sized bird; pale gray overall with black mask. Found in open, dry desert and semidesert areas across Portugal and Spain, into France.

name: Pitt Island Shag
rangeDescription: Chatham islands (new zealand)
description: A small, slender gray shag, with a slender bill, yellow legs and feet, and small dark spots on its shoulder and wing feathers. Feeds, roosts, and breeds around rocky shorelines of the Chatham Islands.

name: Common Crane
rangeDescription: Breeds northern eurasia; winters to northern africa, southern india, and southeastern asia
description: Generally uncommon in open, mainly wild country. Breeds from reedy lakeshores to boggy clearings in boreal forest, winters in wetlands and farmland.

name: Spot-breasted Parrotbill
rangeDescription: Hill forest of assam to eastern myanmar, southern china, and northern indochina
description: A bulbous-headed brown bird with a comically large bill. Brownish overall, with a rich chestnut cap and paler underparts.

name: Cerulean Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Sangihe islands (northeast of sulawesi)
description: An unmistakable, fairly large blue flycatcher confined to Sangihe island. Entirely pale blue, with a paler belly and a conspicuous white eye-ring which is the most striking identification feature.

name: Glossy Ibis
rangeDescription: Locally in eastern north and southern south america, africa, eurasia, to australasia
description: Long, curved bill. Adults mostly dark with iridescent green and reddish tones.

name: Sad Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Open woodland and montane forest of jamaica
description: A woodland species that often perches quietly three to ten meters above the ground; tends to lean forward on its perch. Note its relatively small bill and the lack of rust on the wings and tail.

name: Madeira Chaffinch
rangeDescription: Madeira
description: Dapper little finch endemic to Madeira, where it inhabits a range of habitats, from forests to farmlands. Handsome, brightly colored male has a blue-grayish cowl, pale orangish face and breast, and a black-and-white wing pattern (colors muted in winter).

name: Rondonia Bushbird
rangeDescription: South-central amazonian brazil, in rondônia, southern amazonas, and northern mato grosso
description: Large antbird with a very distinctive, robust upturned bill. Males are all black and females are chestnut with a black throat patch.

name: Biak White-eye
rangeDescription: Mountains of supiori and biak (cenderawasih bay, off northwestern new guinea)
description: A small bird of forest on Biak Island where it is the only white-eye. Olive-green head and back, yellow under the base of the tail, dark gray face, pale gray underparts with whitish throat and belly.
